<a name="UseWriteBuffer"></a>
## func UseWriteBuffer

```go
func UseWriteBuffer(defaultBuffered bool, opts []options.NewFileOption) bool
```

UseWriteBuffer resolves whether local write buffering applies to a file. defaultBuffered is the backend's default for the file's filesystem, and opts are the options passed to NewFile. StreamingWrite and WriteBuffer, as a value or a pointer, are applied in order, so the last one wins.

<a name="WithStreamingWrite"></a>
## func WithStreamingWrite

```go
func WithStreamingWrite() options.NewFileOption
```

WithStreamingWrite returns the StreamingWrite implementation of NewFileOption.

Backends that stage writes in a local temporary file so that Seek or Read can follow Write \(s3, gs, and azure\) skip that local file and stream bytes directly to the remote object. Calling Seek or Read after Write, or Write after Seek or Read, before Close then fails with vfs.ErrWriteBufferDisabled. Backends that do not stage writes ignore the option.

<a name="WithWriteBuffer"></a>
## func WithWriteBuffer

```go
func WithWriteBuffer() options.NewFileOption
```

WithWriteBuffer returns the WriteBuffer implementation of NewFileOption.

It enables local write buffering for a file even when the backend's filesystem options disable it \(for example s3.Options.DisableWriteBuffer\), so that one file can use Write together with Seek or Read. When both WithStreamingWrite and WithWriteBuffer are passed, the last one wins. Backends that do not stage writes ignore the option.
